title: wg: protocol-07 gives a Welcome joiner no defined way to get a distributionService ratchet tree
description:
Found by mimid-jvde (2026-11-21), building decision mimid-1wgh.81.

protocol-07 §5.5 says a Welcome FanoutMessage carries a RatchetTreeOption
(ratchet-tree-options-02 §3), so a hub may send distributionService(4)
("the ratchet_tree is reconstructed by the Distribution Service"). Neither
draft says how the joiner then gets the tree:

1. protocol-07 §5.6 (POST /groupInfo/{roomId}) is the only endpoint that
   returns a tree, and it is written for external joins. It does not say
   that a client holding a Welcome may use it, nor how the hub authorizes
   one: the credential/joiningCode text is about permission to join, while
   the Welcome joiner is already a member in the hub's tree. mimid lets a
   request signed with the key of a current leaf whose identity is the
   requesting credential through without a policy check (mimid-1wgh.81).
2. GroupInfoRequest names no epoch, and the response is the current epoch's.
   A Welcome for epoch N is useless with the tree of N+1, so any Commit
   between the Welcome and the fetch strands the joiner.
3. Size: the GroupInfoResponse carries the same tree (encrypted) as a full
   Welcome, and both travel in one HTTP body, so by-reference only saves the
   Welcome's EncryptedGroupSecrets (about 118 octets per joining client in
   mimid's measurements: Welcome+tree 1117 vs GroupInfo response 1198 octets
   for one client, 2209 vs 1936 for four). Neither draft has a way to fetch a
   tree in parts, so a room whose tree passes the providers' body cap cannot
   take new members by any path.

Possible asks: say in §5.6 that a Welcome joiner may fetch the tree there
(and how it is authorized), let the request name the epoch or the
GroupInfo's tree_hash, or define a tree fetch for the distributionService
case. Raise on the list or as a mimi-protocol issue only with Mark's OK.
